quote: How much panels can you fit in 10 by 23?
stewart_read: This is exactly the kind of closer/design-tier technical question the schema's escape hatch exists for, but the rep engages with 'I'll be honest, I'm not too sure' instead of redirecting to the design team immediately.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep could be strategically building trust by staying honest and present rather than deflecting a highly engaged, analytical customer — deflecting too fast might read as evasive to this specific customer type.
coaching_implication: Coach the universal escape hatch phrasing here: 'That's exactly the kind of layout question our design team nails down with satellite imaging — let's get your bill over so they can run the real numbers.' Use on the first specs question, not the third.

quote: What's your what's the size of your panel? Three by five?
stewart_read: Rep says 'Yeah. I'm pretty sure. Let's see' and audibly starts searching rather than admitting he doesn't carry panel specs and redirecting — a soft version of guessing rather than clean admission-and-recovery.
coaching_implication: Reinforce: when a customer asks for a hard spec number, admit-and-redirect ('that's the design team's exact numbers') is safer than looking one up live, which stalls the call and signals uncertainty.

quote: I'd love to just get your utility bill so we know how many panels you would need, and then just send it over to my design team.
stewart_read: This line is the correct redirect and lands well, but it arrives after roughly three minutes of unstructured panel math that the rep could have shut down on the first ask with the same phrase.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic patience — letting the customer exhaust his own math may have made him more receptive to 'let the design team actually run this' once he saw the manual approach was going nowhere (he does immediately concede 'it's only nine panels... I'm not doing that right').
coaching_implication: Note the eventual success of the redirect, but flag the lost time; same result was likely available three exchanges earlier.

quote: Yeah. So it'll take me two months to get that to you.
stewart_read: Customer reveals he hasn't moved in and won't have real usage data for a month — an unusual scenario the rep handles reasonably by pivoting to square footage, but he never asks whether the customer wants a photo/text of a bill later or sets a plan to collect it before the appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep's square-footage pivot may be an acceptable substitute per protocol since design can start without the bill in some cases, making this a non-issue rather than a miss.
coaching_implication: Confirm with Kenny whether square-footage-only design estimates are an approved substitute for missing bill data, or whether the rep should have set a firm plan to collect the bill closer to the appointment.
